explanations.text:
# FIRST PROJECT USE

if user asks the ai harness for code and project has no human/:
    ai harness [registers the project](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:cmd_init); [the user never types human init](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md)
    if codebase exists, ai harness writes the first global flow in a new human file. if human file name isn't taken by a folder or project, use it.
    [opens the reader link](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:serve_away)
    on the first open,
    if codebase exists:
        ai harness [recommends a new line for a small non-breaking change](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:cmd_tip),
        web [click the compile button](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:showTip)
        [highlights new line](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:tipLine)
        a green handwritten looking arrow and a "This is a new change" floats and points to the recommended line.
    else:
        [use the defaeult human file](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:First use), [add the abstraction](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:cmd_tip) "web with lots of animations that explain how human works", 
        [highlight the green compile button](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:showTip).
        a green handwritten looking arrow and a "This is human code" floats and [points to the abstraction text](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:tipFirst)
if user goes on asking for code by chat and not through human:
    [ai harness refuses](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md)
    gives the reader link
    explains shortly how human works



# USER WRITES ABSTRACTION

if user gives abstraction to ai harness, ai registers the project first, using "human init":
    sweeps the tree through the ignore sieve,
    writes the file list into human/human.json,
    if no project_id: create,
    create reader files,
    create first human file.

ai harness runs "human map <human file> --verbatim <abstraction>"
accept pins in the abstraction but refuse if abstraction's pins point to no real code or abstraction

abstraction gets flagged as the user's and keeps that first copy, without the pins, in "origin" atribute
ai harness writes the code files, no comments. making sure the file must parse.

if code exist: sync code lines and pins
if code was changed first or other abstractions get stale: sync the abstractions

refuse if there's a cycle in the maps

if no pins in abstraction:
  ai harness retexts abstraction to include the pins
  refuse if abstraction changes after adding pins



# USER EDITS ABSTRACTION

user edits abstraction
if edit comes through web, server runs "human retext --verbatim":
  change abstraction,
  marks stale the abstractions linked to old abstractions;


ai harness [compares old and the new abstraction for the program](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md)
ai harness decides and writes the new code based on the human abstraction.

ai harness runs "human retext":
  accept pins in the abstraction but refuse if abstraction's pins point to no real code or abstraction
  sync code lines and pins
  if code was changed first or other abstractions get stale: sync the abstractions
